# Churn definition

Churn rate for a given month is calculated as:

Churn Rate = Customers Lost During the Month / Customers at the Start of the Month

A customer counts as "lost" if they cancel both Atlas and Beacon and do not
resubscribe within 30 days.

Churn matters for revenue because Subscription Revenue is just the sum of
active plan fees that month. When a customer churns, their plan fee s

an fees that month. When a customer churns, their plan fee stops
being counted the very next month, so a higher churn rate directly lowers
next month's Subscription Revenue - and therefore lowers total revenue, as
described in the revenue recognition update.

# Company overview

SB Company builds software that helps mid-size retailers plan and track
inventory. We sell two products, Atlas and Beacon (see their product pages),
and we've been operating since 2021.

We earn money in two main ways: monthly subscription fees for Atlas and

# Office and support

SB Company's main office is at 400 Harbor Way, Suite 210, Oakland, CA. Most
of the team works from there a few days a week.

If you're a customer with an urgent issue, our support team's SLA is to
respond to critical tickets within 4 business hours. Everything else in
this document is just general onboarding info for new hires and isn't
related to product functionality.

# Atlas

Atlas is SB Company's inventory planning product. It forecasts how much
stock a retailer should order for the next month based on past sales, and
flags items that are likely to run out or overstock.

Atlas is sold as a monthly subscription, priced per store location. Most
customers connect Atlas to their point-of-sale system so forecasts update
automatically each night.

# Beacon

Beacon is SB Company's inventory tracking product. It gives retailers a
live view of stock levels across all their store locations and warehouses,
and alerts staff when an item's count looks wrong.

Beacon is also sold as a monthly subscription. Customers who process a
large volume of stock updates each day may go over their plan's included

# Revenue recognition policy

This is the original policy, written when SB Company only tracked two
revenue components.

Total revenue for a given month is calculated as:

Total Revenue = Subscription Revenue + Usage Revenue

- **Subscription Revenue** is the sum of active monthly plan fees for every
  customer on Atlas or Beacon that month.
- **Usage Revenue** is the sum of overage charges billed

th.
- **Usage Revenue** is the sum of overage charges billed when a customer's
  data processing goes over their plan's included amount.

See the revenue recognition update for a newer version of this formula.

# Revenue recognition policy update

As of November 2025, finance updated how total revenue is calculated. This
replaces the formula in the original revenue recognition policy.

Total Revenue = Subscription Revenue + Usage Revenue + Add-on Revenue - Refunds

- **Add-on Revenue** is new: it's the sum of one-time purchases for extra
  features, like advanced reporting.
- **Refunds** are now subtract

res, like advanced reporting.
- **Refunds** are now subtracted in the same month they are issued, instead
  of being handled as a separate line item later.

Subscription Revenue and Usage Revenue are calculated the same way as
before; see the original policy for those definitions. Note that
Subscription Revenue is sensitive to customer churn - see the churn
definition for how the two relate.
